translation: As for thirst from disease caused by malaria, the Nüe Lun (瘧論) says: When yang is excessive, there is external heat; when yin is deficient, there is internal heat; when both internal and external are hot, then one pants and is thirsty, and therefore wishes to drink cold. Now when yang-excess and yin-deficiency produce disease-heat, the proper method is to use cold drugs to nourish yin and drain heat; this is the way of draining the excess and supplementing the decline. As for thirst from rich, sweet food and mineral drugs, the Qi Bing Lun (奇病論) says: There is one with a sweet mouth; what is the name of the disease? Qibo said: This is what overflows from the five qi (五氣); the name of the disease is spleen dan (脾癉).
translator_notes: 瘧論/奇病論 kept as chapter names; 脾癉 rendered 'spleen dan'; 五氣 rendered 'five qi'.
